name: Recode Studios Ltd
title: Recode Studios Ltd - 544755 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

read.thesis: Asset-light beauty brand reports FY26 revenue ₹80 cr (+67%) and PAT ₹11.22 cr, but the IPO cash is funding working capital (receivables ~₹15 cr vs ₹8 cr) and management gave no supply-side or pricing evidence, with 50% growth guided without numbers for the quarter.

summary.headline: FY26 revenue rose 67% to ₹80 crore and PAT rose 260% to ₹11.22 crore, with management guiding for at least 50% growth in 2027.
summary.overview: Recode Studios held its first post-IPO earnings call covering H2 and FY26 on 3 June 2026. Management reported FY26 revenue of ₹80 crore (FY25: ₹48 crore), EBITDA of ₹16 crore (FY25: ₹6 crore) and PAT of ₹11.22 crore (FY25: ₹3.11 crore). H2 FY26 revenue was ₹43 crore against ₹29 crore in H2 FY25. The company has shifted from FOFO franchise stores to dark stores run by third parties, and is building modern trade, quick commerce and a Ludhiana warehouse. Several answers on CAC, receivables and repeat-purchase data were vague or deferred.

financial_highlights.change: vs 13% in FY25 (CFO); analyst cited 21% for full year

financial_highlights.metric: EBITDA margin H1 vs H2 FY26

segments.name: Online (D2C website and marketplaces)
segments.commentary: Online is about 60% of sales versus 40% offline, per management. Own website is about 50% of online sales, roughly 20-22% of total revenue as per analyst arithmetic that management accepted. Over 70% of online revenue is from own website per opening remarks; these two figures are not reconciled.

segments.name: B2B (incl. Nykaa)
segments.commentary: Nykaa is treated as B2B because it buys inventory upfront on a sale-or-return basis. Management did not give Nykaa's revenue share. Amazon, Flipkart and Myntra are classed as D2C.

segments.name: Offline / FOFO and COCO stores
segments.commentary: 22 stores: 3 COCO and 19 FOFO. FOFO franchise model is now closed; new stores are dark stores run by third-party operators. FOFO stores also act as regional distributors.

guidance_outlook: Targeting at least 50% revenue growth in 2027, with hopes to achieve it in H1 as well.
Management said the 50% CAGR and similar margins can be sustained for the next 3 years when asked by an investor.
EBITDA margin expected to stay near FY26 levels (about 20%) for 2-3 years; no near-term expansion as extra profit will go into marketing.
Online/offline split expected to move toward 50:50 this fiscal year, with offline growing faster.
Marketing spend guideline held at 20% of revenue.
Ludhiana warehouse expected to commence operations from April 2027.
Modern trade vertical with its own team to be set up in 10-15 days; Shoppers Stop, Lifestyle and Dabur New are priority accounts.
Quick commerce entry (own service plus platforms) expected within 1-2 months, though management called the category loss-making.
capex_capacity: 22 stores in total: 3 COCO and 19 FOFO, plus six warehouses and dark stores.
Dark stores opened in Jabalpur, Hyderabad and Chennai; Bhubaneswar and Ranchi in pipeline.
First modern trade kiosk opened at Omaxe Mall, New Delhi, a few days before the call; more malls in discussion.
Ludhiana warehouse, the main hub for all channels, planned to start from April 2027.
IPO proceeds are mainly for working capital and inventory build-up; no specific capex figure given.
demand_pricing: Management said the beauty and personal care market CAGR is 6-8%, and that its own 50% growth is backed by demand seen over the last two months.
Pricing and product mix moving up: new launches carry MRPs of ₹999, ₹1,500 and ₹2,500, versus earlier ₹200-300.
About 20-25 new products in the pipeline for launch over the next six months; management did not give an annual launch count.
Month-on-month online repeat rate about 40%; AOV up about ₹100 (for example ₹700 to ₹800). Multi-year repeat data was not available.
Management said 4-5 products are market leaders, such as a setting spray and primer.
Management said it positions itself as affordable luxury and mass premium, benchmarking against international brands rather than Indian peers.
Management said H1 is seasonally weak for colour cosmetics, with growth coming from OND (October to December) and festive months.

qa_highlights.question: Is the company asset-heavy or asset-light, and how will the channel mix look over 2-3 years?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it will stay asset-light. Online is about 60% and offline 40%, moving toward 50:50 this fiscal year, with offline growing faster. Focus is on South and Central India, where a team has been hired.

qa_highlights.question: Will the EBITDA margin hold given the channel shift and H1/H2 seasonality?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said margins are similar across online and offline, so EBITDA margin should stay consistent. It said H1 is seasonally weaker and that margin improvement is not planned because extra profit will go into marketing.

qa_highlights.question: How is CAC tracked, and is the 20% marketing spend ongoing?
qa_highlights.answer: CAC is not defined per customer because sales come from Meta, Google, marketplaces and offline. Management said it will keep spending 20% of revenue on advertising.

qa_highlights.question: Why are FOFO stores being replaced and how are franchisees compensated?
qa_highlights.answer: FOFO model is closed; dark stores run by third parties are being opened to save rent. Management said FOFO stores earn ₹4-5 lakh a month from footfall and distribution and that no franchisee has closed except one where the mall shut down. Franchise payback had been set at 22 months.

qa_highlights.question: Why did receivables rise to about ₹15 crore from ₹8 crore, and what are payment cycles?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Nykaa pays in about 2-3 months and sometimes up to 120 days. FOFO stores buy on credit and pay as they sell, so working capital is needed. It could not give an exact channel-wise breakdown.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for quick commerce and its margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is on Blinkit in Delhi NCR and listed on Zepto and Swiggy about 1.5 years ago, but has limited presence. It will not spend ₹200 to sell ₹100, and is building its own quick commerce delivery; management called quick commerce loss-making for players like Recode.

qa_highlights.question: How is sourcing affected by geopolitics and currency?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Gulf tensions have less impact than during earlier disruptions. Kajal is sourced from Germany and foundation from Thailand, and Indian sourcing may rise slightly, but no INR impact figure was given.

risks_watch: Working capital: receivables rose to about ₹15 crore from ₹8 crore (analyst's figure); payment cycles from Nykaa run up to 120 days, and FOFO credit is extended to partners.
Management was unable to provide CAC, channel-level receivables or multi-year repeat data; it said it would share data later.
Dependence on Nykaa and other marketplaces, with Nykaa booked as B2B on sale-or-return terms.
Quick commerce entry, which management itself called loss-making; the dark store model and third-party operators need monitoring.
Third-party manufacturing and labelling, with quality checks at batch filling; no quality issues disclosed.
Ludhiana warehouse timing (April 2027) and modern trade ramp-up with dedicated team.
Inconsistent figures: 70% online revenue from own website vs 20-22% of total revenue; EBITDA margin 20% vs 21% cited on the call.
summary.management_tone: Confident and promotional on growth and profitability, with a firm 50% growth target. Evasive or deferred on CAC, channel receivables, repeat-customer data and dark store economics, which were pushed to one-on-one follow-ups.
key_quotes: We are targeting at least 50% growth in 2027 and we are hoping to achieve this number in H1 as well, backed by demand momentum, deeper market penetration, new channels, and an expanding distribution network.
Recode is a replacement for international brands.
Nowhere in the world will a customer return to you without quality.
Quick commerce is currently a loss-making venture; we are still working on that.

adds.what: Ludhiana warehouse, main hub for all channels
Dark stores in Bhubaneswar and Ranchi (pipeline)
Modern trade kiosks at malls, first opened at Omaxe Mall New Delhi; more malls in discussion

growth.why: Management targets at least 50% revenue growth in FY27 (hoping for H1 too) and says it is backed by demand seen over the last two months, a 40% MoM repeat rate and 20-25 products in the pipeline, but no firm order or capacity numbers were given beyond a Ludhiana warehouse from April 2027 with no capex figure.
